one_liner: Go WAL library storing append-only logs on S3/object storage or local disk; vendor test shows 3.5-5.8x Kafka single-stream write throughput
what_it_does: Woodpecker is the write-ahead log that replaced Kafka/Pulsar inside Milvus 2.6: named, strictly ordered append-only logs with one exclusive writer and any number of readers, persisted as segment files on S3-compatible object storage (MinIO, AWS S3, GCS, Azure Blob, Aliyun OSS, Tencent COS) or a local filesystem, with all metadata and coordination in etcd. It runs either embedded in your Go process (client plus LogStore in-process, the docs' 'MemoryBuffer' mode) or as a separate LogStore cluster that replicates each write to a 3- or 5-node quorum before offloading to object storage ('QuorumBuffer'/service mode). The API is its own Go interface (CreateLog/OpenLog, LogWriter.Write/WriteAsync, LogReader.ReadNext, Truncate), not the Kafka protocol: no topics/partitions, consumer groups or broker-side features.
how_it_is_fast: Group commit: appends land in an in-memory sequential buffer (entries ordered by id, gaps held back) that is flushed when it hits an entry/byte cap or a timer (defaults 200 ms for object storage, 10 ms for local FS, 1 ms in service mode), turning many small writes into large sequential ones. On object storage each flush is cut into ~2 MB blocks uploaded as separate objects in parallel from a goroutine pool (maxFlushThreads, default 32) while acks are still released strictly in entry order; blocks of a sealed segment are later compacted into merged objects (up to segmentCompactionPolicy.maxBytes, default 2 MB). Local-FS mode appends CRC32-framed records to one segment file and fsyncs once per flushed block. Writer fencing uses object-store conditional PUT (If-None-Match) instead of lock round-trips where the backend supports it; the vendor frames the result as reaching 60-80% of each backend's raw bandwidth.
when_to_use: A Go system (vector DB, database, event-sourced service) that needs an ordered, durable WAL and already runs etcd plus S3/MinIO, and you want to stop operating a Kafka or Pulsar cluster for it.
Bulk single-stream appends to S3 where ~100-200 ms commit latency is fine: the vendor measured 750 MB/s from one client/stream vs 130 MB/s for Kafka.
Single-node deployments on local disk that want fsync-acknowledged appends at millisecond latency (vendor: 450 MB/s at 1.8 ms).
Log retention priced at object-storage rates with stateless compute, where catch-up/replay reads can come straight from object storage.
Multi-AZ durability via the 3-replica quorum service mode (ack after 2 of 3 replicas, async flush to object storage), if you can run the extra LogStore service.
when_not_to_use: You need the Kafka API or ecosystem (wire protocol, partitions, consumer groups, Connect/Streams, transactions): none of it exists here.

Latency-sensitive writes over object storage: the vendor's own table shows S3/MinIO modes at 166/184 ms vs Kafka 58 ms and Pulsar 35 ms, and the Milvus docs put embedded MemoryBuffer mode at 200-500 ms.
Self-hosted MinIO backends: the same table has Woodpecker at 71 MB/s, about half of Kafka's 130 MB/s.
Many concurrent producers into one log: each log has one exclusive writer (etcd session lock or conditional-write fence); in lock mode failover can wait up to the 10 s session TTL.
Risk-averse production outside Milvus: still v0.1.x, and a quorum-mode bug that lost acknowledged data after compaction (#320) was only fixed in September 2026.

integration.dependencies: etcd (required; only metadata backend supported) plus an S3-compatible object store or local filesystem; Go deps include minio-go, Azure SDK, etcd client/server v3.5, gRPC, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, zap and hashicorp/memberlist (service-mode gossip). Service mode also ships a LogStore server, Docker images, a Kubernetes operator and the wpcli admin tool.
integration.platforms: Pure Go; Docker build images target Linux only (Ubuntu 20.04/22.04, Rocky Linux 8, Amazon Linux 2023); other OSes not documented
integration.thread_safety: Not documented per method. Cluster-wide there is one exclusive LogWriter per log, enforced by an etcd session lock or conditional-write fence; WriteAsync returns a per-message result channel; multiple independent readers per log are supported.

gotchas: License trap: the embedded client (woodpecker/client/logstore_client_local.go) imports the server/ package, which is AGPL-3.0-only or SSPL-1.0, so embedded mode compiles copyleft code into your binary; only the non-server packages are Apache-2.0.

Writers can be invalidated under you: when the etcd session expires writes fail with ErrLogWriterLockLost and the app must reopen a writer. With fencePolicy 'auto' on a new cluster, startup fails outright if the object store's conditional-write check fails; there is no silent fallback to locks.

Docs lag code: the README reader example calls OpenLogReader(ctx, start), but the interface is now OpenLogReader(ctx, from, readerBaseName), and the README config shows 4 MB flushes / 64 threads while current defaults are 2 MB / 32.
Open reader issues: ReadNext keeps serving data after the reader is closed (#277), and an idle tail reader polls etcd plus a quorum-wide RPC every 200 ms (#352).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No siblings catalogued yet. Against the Kafka baseline, pick it only when you want an embeddable Go WAL on object storage rather than a general-purpose broker.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party single-node, single-client, single-log-stream write test, published identically in the README, the Milvus docs and a May 2025 Milvus blog post. Woodpecker to local FS: 450 MB/s at 1.8 ms; to S3: 750 MB/s at 166 ms; to MinIO: 71 MB/s at 184 ms. Kafka: 129.96 MB/s at 58 ms; Pulsar: 107 MB/s at 35 ms. No CPU or instance type (only 'single EC2 instance' for the S3 ceiling), message size, batching, Go version, or Kafka/Pulsar settings (acks, fsync, replication) are given, the repo has no Kafka/Pulsar harness, and the numbers come from early-2025 development builds.
status_note: Actively developed (v0.1.45 released 2026-09-21, releases roughly weekly) and shipped as the default WAL in Milvus 2.6+, but still pre-1.0. Client packages are Apache-2.0 and server/ is AGPL-3.0/SSPL, so embedding it in proprietary software needs legal review.
